conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Ah, a murder case?" This clue far exceeded previous expectations, leaving them shocked as well.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Look at the photo.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What does this have to do with Haddin?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: In the photo, a man in police uniform lies on the ground, his chest soaked with blood; another man in plain clothes kneels beside him, seemingly searching his chest. Although the photo appears to have been taken at night without flash, the details are presented nearly perfectly under the illumination of the police car's headlights.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison remains silent, observing these clues.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Who took this photo?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Who took this photo?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "This photo was mailed to me on June 30th. The envelope had no signature but was marked for Redman—that is, me—to open personally. I was also very surprised when I opened it. Because no witnesses were found in the previous police and prosecutor's investigation, yet this mysterious photo is not only very clear but also directly provides a new lead."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "This photo arrived at quite the opportune time."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Being able to capture a photo from this angle and sending it to the prosecutor's office after such a long time, it's highly likely the photo was taken by an accomplice who wanted to harm Haddin due to internal strife."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I have no expertise in photography; perhaps you can glean some clues from the photo?"

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled in many areas.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Amateur Alison tries to look.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and are you now betting on the untraceable one?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You are all clueless about photography.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "...To be honest, we are also currently tracking Haddin's whereabouts. As for the public warrant, my suggestion is to delay it to avoid alerting the target." After a pause, "Based on this photo and the clues we have, this should be a murder."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Photography check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "In that case, I'll proceed as planned. Annie wasn't keen on this plan anyway."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Haddin might be involved with multiple parties; the situation is complex. Some of them are very unfavorable to him."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I think the sender's intention in mailing you the photo was precisely to have you issue a public warrant for him, making it difficult for him to hide and forcing him to reveal his whereabouts."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Speaking of that lecture you mentioned, that was back in January, right? It was a large professional lecture for prosecutors, judges, and lawyers. It's been too long; I don't really remember."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I saw in the file that the murdered officer was investigating former Nazi officials' crimes. Haddin is extremely interested in Nazis. I wonder if you have any leads regarding this aspect?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No, no, I have no impression of Haddin. Otherwise, I would have recognized him the moment I saw the photo."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I wonder if the victim had any family. The previous investigation should have included the victim's activities and social connections from his final period."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "If you need the photo, you can take a copy. I'm sorry, but the original cannot be given to you; it's already archived at the prosecutor's office."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We are very interested in the content of his last investigation into Nazi crimes."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then take a copy of this photo.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Schultz was indeed privately investigating Nazis. This wasn't part of his official duties. The customs section he belonged to is, to my knowledge, the most fair and diligent department. They have cracked several major smuggling cases in the past six months."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: It seems we need to visit the customs section.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Perhaps you could ask his colleagues about Schultz's relatives. They have clearly stated they do not wish to be disturbed further, so unfortunately..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We may need an official reason to question the officers in the Anti-Smuggling Division," David hinted.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hmm... Well then, I can provide two documents with the word 'Search Warrant' written on them."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Thank you for the valuable clues and assistance."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also expressed sincere gratitude.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Redman rummaged through his desk drawer and pulled out two sheets of paper.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Of course, we will use your assistance with discretion."

conversation.speaker: player2

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Head to the Anti-Smuggling Division.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After leaving the Prosecutor's Office, you went to the police station. After presenting Redman's search warrant, Andreas Rilke, the Section Chief of the Anti-Smuggling Division, received you.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We want to understand Mr. Schultz's work during his lifetime, especially anything related to neo-Nazis."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "That's unfortunate. Schultz's investigations into Nazis were entirely based on his personal interest. In other words, he was a volunteer Nazi hunter, and we don't know more either."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "This might be related to his death in the line of duty and is an important lead. Why was he so passionate about this?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The primary duty of the Anti-Smuggling Division is to combat smuggling syndicates. I thought Prosecutor Hermann was fully aware of this before. Why bring it up again now?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It's truly regrettable to lose such a police officer. There have been new developments in the case of his murder. We hope to investigate his belongings to see if we can find more clues." Alison stepped forward with a friendly smile.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "There's been a breakthrough in the evidence recently."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "So you're saying the work of the Anti-Smuggling Division doesn't overlap with neo-Nazi organizations, correct?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "On an official level, the Federal Court has been committed to advancing the pursuit and trial of Nazi war criminals. On a civilian level, volunteer organizations dedicated to hunting down remaining Nazi elements are constantly emerging."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David pondered these words for a moment, feeling Rilke wasn't very concerned about this matter. "Then we'd like to understand the situation on the day of the incident. The victim wasn't on duty at the time. Who recalled him temporarily and for what reason?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Do you really think Schultz's personal belongings would still be here? Sorry, the case happened over two months ago. His personal effects were taken away by his relatives long ago."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David wants to gauge Rilke's attitude towards Schultz. He really doesn't seem like a superior who lost a capable subordinate.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: As soon as David's words left his mouth, Rilke's expression changed slightly. After a brief silence, his eyes narrowed a little. "Sorry, scheduling matters are internal affairs of the Anti-Smuggling Division! The Anti-Smuggling Division is the hardest-working and most incorruptible department in all of Frankfurt. It's normal to have temporary work arrangements requiring overtime. No comment!"

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and at this moment, will you gamble on the one with no trace to follow?

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Oh ho, after seeing the change in Rilke's expression, he showed an intrigued look. Is it really that incorruptible?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You feel that although Rilke appears concerned on the surface, it's somewhat insincere posturing.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Rilke's attitude made Alison somewhat suspicious. There's definitely more to this than meets the eye.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The entire police station is working hard on this case. Not everyone is willing to waste time on such pointless questioning. If you want to continue playing guessing games here, we don't have time to entertain you!"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We came here for Schultz, who died in the line of duty! You can't treat us like this!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Two tall, burly policemen rushed in, one hand on the baton at their waist. "Please leave the police station!"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew yelled a couple of times at the top of his lungs.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Using the cover of others in front, turn on the eavesdropping device, then plop down on the sofa, casually stuffing the device into a sofa crevice.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Get lost, now!" A police officer was already growing impatient, pressing his baton against Andrew's chest.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Alright, alright, we're leaving."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Hurriedly push Andrew to leave. Let's go, let's go, don't linger.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "If you don't leave now, I won't be able to consider Prosecutor Redman's face anymore. Are you trying to assault an officer?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: While walking out, observe the reactions of the Customs Investigation Section staff. "We're all on the same side, no need for such roughness."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We were just asking routine questions, is this really necessary?" Unwillingly, slowly get up and shuffle away.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Rilke indignantly directs the police to escort you out. The Customs Investigation Section clerks are somewhat baffled, but obviously no one would be foolish enough to clash with the Section Chief for a few people of unknown origin.

conversation.speaker: player6

One of us will watch the bureau entrance, another will keep an eye on the surroundings, and we'll stay in radio contact."

conversation.text: Then Alison and Johnsen drive to the address of the Mirror Newspaper recorded on the letter. It shouldn't be off-work time yet, right?

conversation.speaker: player3

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: While chatting with Jackson, you learn that the Mirror Newspaper is a publication that started after World War II. Although its history isn't long, it holds a significant market share in Frankfurt. It mainly reports local news, documenting all aspects of Frankfurt city post-WWII. In terms of written content, it's practically Frankfurt's "encyclopedia." Locals even prioritize checking the newspaper building's library and archives over the Frankfurt Library when searching for local information. The two of you successfully arrive at the Mirror Newspaper building, an impressive Bauhaus-style structure.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Compare this. Is it similar in outline to the Haddin building plans?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The sketch obtained from the lines only has a few incomplete parts. The embassy could be ruled out because it was small and simple enough to be obviously mismatched with the sketch at a glance. Right now, you can't tell at all whether it looks similar or not.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Before getting out of the car, David checks for any surveillance. After confirming it's safe, he gets out and enters the newspaper building.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Watch for any tails. Check your equipment. Enter the building discreetly.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Inside the building, people come and go. No one pays you any attention. Many citizens are browsing in the library and archives.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Find a staff member, state your purpose, and ask where you should go to visit this journalist.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: A passing journalist hurriedly tells you Margaret Young's office location before continuing to dash upstairs.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Go find her office.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Follow Alison.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Margaret greeted you. She was a Caucasian woman of average height, wearing a dark brown professional suit; she had beautiful shoulder-length brown hair with a slight natural curl; her features were delicate, and she wore a faint smile, exuding a lively and approachable youthful aura; yet, one could still see the faint dark circles under her eyes that she tried hard to conceal, perhaps caused by long nights of writing. "Hello, I don't believe we've met before, right?" "Do you have some news leads to tell me?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David followed a step behind Alison, closing the door as their conversation began.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Present the disguised identity from the Foreign Office, smile. "Sorry for the sudden visit. We are Mr. Haddin's colleagues. He seems to have encountered some problems recently. We learned he has been corresponding with you and hope to understand his situation from you."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "He might not be safe right now. We need your support."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Margaret stared into your eyes, clearly weighing whether to trust you. Finally, she nodded, her tone gentle but alert: "It's not convenient here. Please follow me."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Follow her.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David followed cautiously.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Margaret left her workstation and led you to a small room near the stairs. Along the way, you could see her workstation was neat and orderly, typical of a strong career woman, with tidy files and her camera beside them.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Mentally express sincere admiration for such an outstanding woman.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Alright, it's quieter here. No one usually comes. May I ask how you knew Mr. Haddin and I were corresponding?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Let Alison speak. Communication between women is more likely to build trust.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We found your letters among the things he left behind, confirming you were his helper. That's why we came to you." Alison appeared very sincere.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Things he left behind? Sigh, it seems Mr. Haddin received my warning. I hope he's safe."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "He seems to have commissioned you to investigate something, and you warned him. We want to know, what exactly is threatening our colleague?" "Although Haddin is not in good health, he has been a great help to others in his work."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "That's a long story. On the evening of June 30th, after meeting Mr. Haddin, out of curiosity, I followed him and saw him meet with another group of unidentified individuals; after their meeting ended, I decided to continue following those 'mysterious figures'—in such a situation, no journalist could suppress their curiosity. I overheard their conversation: they believed Haddin had 'defected' and were going to eliminate him. Realizing the extreme danger, I immediately went to Mr. Haddin's residence but couldn't find him. I had to write a letter and put it in his mailbox, hoping he would receive the message and be aware of the danger."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison looked at her with a grave expression, actually observing her micro-expressions, hoping to use psychology to judge if her words concealed anything or if she was lying.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Psychology check result: D100=40/75 Success. Move forward quickly, be decisive. No danger ahead.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gray felt the other party was very sincere.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Goodness, how could he encounter such a thing... Do you know the specific identity of that organization? Also, could you tell us what Mr. Haddin commissioned you to investigate? It's very important for us to understand his situation." Alison appeared shocked and then urgently expressed concern for her colleague.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Did you call Haddin on the afternoon of the 30th?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No, after I heard their plan to eliminate Haddin, I immediately left to notify Mr. Haddin." "No, Mr. Haddin is a man of strong sense of justice but somewhat mysterious. He didn't leave me contact information; he only called me unilaterally." "Regarding Mr. Haddin's commission, it's like this: I've published some investigative reports on Nazi fugitives. Mr. Haddin proactively approached me expressing willingness to cooperate in the investigation; he never mentioned his own identity, only said he was British; I thought he had a strong sense of justice, so I helped him organize some materials, and we met a few times afterward."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, he was very concerned about this area... Do you have backups of these materials? It might help us understand who wants to harm him."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Of course, they are all clues and related investigations about where Nazi fugitives fled to. You can make copies later. Since you are Mr. Haddin's colleagues, have you seen any strange people coming to see Haddin?" "I think since Mr. Haddin is part of a mysterious organization, he must have had dealings with the organization."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "No, I think generally strange people wouldn't dare to come to a place like the embassy casually. We indeed know less about this aspect than you do."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Or, aside from social activities with colleagues, did he go to any unusual places?" "Also, regarding Mr. Haddin's correspondence, did anyone else go to his residence to look for him?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "He loved reading and also went to the Frankfurt library. I wonder if he ever came to the newspaper's library and archives room?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Haddin was not in good health and hardly participated in social activities. To be honest, we don't know much about this helpful colleague's private life."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "He did come, but only to check some reports on Nazi activities in Frankfurt. He didn't interact much with others. Did he know anyone at the Frankfurt library?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We will go there to ask later. Your enthusiasm and thoughtfulness are truly touching." Alison bowed her head to express gratitude.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David shook his head, indicating he didn't know either. "You should also be careful about your own safety."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Please also be careful not to blindly seek help from the authorities. There are Nazi sympathizers among the police and judicial officials. Many former Nazi war criminals have not only escaped prosecution but have also climbed to high positions."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "What are you saying? There are Nazi sympathizers among the police and judicial officials too?" Alison was very shocked but immediately lowered her voice. "No wonder Haddin encountered such things... We will definitely keep it secret. You have helped us so much; we cannot put you at risk."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also gave her his assurance.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You must have seen my contact information on the letter. We can contact each other by phone if anything comes up later."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Thank you very much for your help. If things are resolved smoothly, we will come to thank you in person." Alison shook her hand.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also shook hands with this principled lady.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Make copies of Haddin's materials, then go to the archives room to look.

After Haddin left, the mysterious individuals went behind the café to smoke and discussed how to deal with Haddin. Margaret eavesdropped by the wall and heard their plan.

conversation.speaker: player3

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "How could this be!......"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Secretly taken by a professional... Who would do such a thing..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "If this photo is real, it's hard to imagine such a shocking photo not being used as a front-page news headline."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, we also find it strange what the purpose of sending such a photo at this time is. The police officer in the photo seems to belong to the Customs Investigation Bureau. Do you know anything about them?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "If it's a forgery, the other party's skill must be extremely high. I can't easily determine the authenticity of this photo because yours is also a reprint."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We are completely clueless about photography. Thank you for your analysis."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I've also heard about the struggle between the Customs Investigation Bureau and smuggling syndicates. After the war, the largest smuggling syndicate in the Frankfurt city area was 'Hermes,' but in the past six months, it has been heavily cracked down by customs police and retreated to the Aschaffenburg district. It has been replaced by a new smuggling syndicate called the 'Freikorps.'"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "What do you know about neo-Nazi organizations? Do they have any connections with smuggling syndicates?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The Thule Tradition Association is the most rampant neo-Nazi organization in Frankfurt, promoting extreme nationalism. The police have been cracking down on them in recent years."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David nodded. "Then, do you know about anti-Nazi volunteer organizations?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Those who hunt Nazis are usually small, closely-knit groups. They don't formally register because they might face retaliation. But some organizations do carry out related activities. For example, the South German Civil Radio Association often holds 'interesting' themed team-building activities to increase member participation, like investigating radio clues about underground Nazis."
